channel.title: AstroAlert – what's happening in space
channel.description: A daily updated guide to astronomical and space events: eclipses, conjunctions, meteor showers, rocket launches, aurorae and close approaches of asteroids.

item.title: The Moon meets Venus
item.description:
30.12.2027, 23:17 UTC

The Moon passes just 2.9° from Venus – the pair is visible in the evening, after sunset, in Capricornus. The brightest point in the sky after the Sun and the Moon. A striking naked-eye sight and a rewarding subject for a short telephoto lens.

item.title: Falcon 9 Block 5 | SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer D
item.description:
31.12.2026, 00:00 UTC

Launch of Falcon 9 Block 5, operated by SpaceX. Site: Vandenberg SFB, CA, USA. Schedule status: date to be determined. Mission: Tranche 1 Transport Layer D is one of six missions by the United States Space Force Space Development Agency (SDA) for the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA) Tranche 1 Transport Layer constellation, which will provide assured, resilient, low-latency military data and connectivity worldwide to the full range of warfighter platforms from Low Earth Orbit satellites. The constellation will be interconnected with Optical Inter-Satellite Links (OISLs) which have significantly increased performance over existing radio frequency crosslinks. It is expected to operate over Ka band, have stereo coverage and be dynamically networked for simpler hand-offs, greater bandwidth and fault tolerance. item.title: Close approach of asteroid 2019 XF2
item.description:
04.12.2026, 00:35 UTC

An asteroid with an estimated diameter of 10–23 m will pass Earth at 1.19 million km, or 3.1 times the Earth–Moon distance, travelling at 10.2 km/s. For scale: an object this size would burn up in the atmosphere as a bright fireball. This is one of the closer approaches of the week. The pass is entirely safe – approaches like this happen regularly and are tracked as a matter of routine.

item.title: Ursids meteor shower peak
item.description:
22.12.2027, 02:00 UTC

A modest but convenient shower – the radiant is circumpolar, so it is up all night. At maximum, up to 10 meteors per hour in theory (the ZHR – under a perfectly dark sky with the radiant overhead; in practice usually several times fewer). The radiant lies in Ursa Minor. A Moon 32% illuminated will brighten the sky a little. No equipment needed – just a reclining chair, warm clothes and a spot away from city lights.

item.title: Geminids meteor shower peak
item.description:
14.12.2027, 02:00 UTC

The richest shower of the year and the only major one born not from a comet but from asteroid 3200 Phaethon. Its meteors are slow and often colourful. At maximum, up to 150 meteors per hour in theory (the ZHR – under a perfectly dark sky with the radiant overhead; in practice usually several times fewer). The radiant lies in Gemini. Unfortunately the Moon will be 100% illuminated and will drown out the fainter meteors – it is worth observing after it sets. No equipment needed – just a reclining chair, warm clothes and a spot away from city lights.

item.title: Falcon 9 Block 5 | CHORUS
item.description:
04.12.2026, 12:55 UTC

Launch of Falcon 9 Block 5, operated by SpaceX. Site: Cape Canaveral SFS, FL, USA. Schedule status: confirmed. Mission: CHORUS is MDA's next generation Earth observation constellation, consisting of 2 radar satellites (C-band SAR and X-band SAR), in a 53.5 degree 600 km altitude LEO, with the X-band trailing the C-band by 60 minutes. A collaborative multi-sensor constellation, CHORUS will bring together diverse and unique imagery and data sources and provide a new level of near real-time insight and innovative Earth observation services. Operating in a unique mid-inclination orbit, CHORUS will be able to image day or night, regardless of weather conditions, with daily access of up to 95% of the coverage area. From an industry-leading 700km-wide imaging swath down to sub-metre high resolution, CHORUS will provide the most extensive and unrivalled Earth observation radar imaging capacity available on the market in a single mission. Also on board this mission are 2 satellites from ICEYE and PECCY. Launch dates slip often – check the current status before tuning into a webcast.

Mission details

item.description:
